data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old Norse name Halvarr, composed of háls (health, good health) and varr (guardian, protector). In Norse mythology, Hallvard may have been associated with the god Tyr, who was a god of war and protection. The name Hallvard is a strong and courageous name for a baby boy. The name Hallvard carries the meaning “Ruler of the brave” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hallvard usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of the brave and live with faith, good character and purpose.
